description: Fig. 6 is a composite, multi-panel figure of machine-learning screening maps for FeMnAlC austenitic low-density steel, all drawn within the 30 wt.% Mn search space. Five panels (a)–(e) share identical axes: x = Al(wt.%), roughly 1.5–12.5 with ticks at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12; y = C(wt.%), 0.0–2.2 with ticks every 0.2. Each panel is a dense grid of marker points coloured red (criterion satisfied) or blue/black (not satisfied), headed by a red-circle legend entry. (a) maps "The existence of the κ phase (Y₁)": red for Al above roughly 5 wt.% at essentially all C, blue below — a near-vertical boundary. (b) maps "A γ+κ dual-phase region at 500–600 °C (Y₂)": only a small red island centred near Al 6–9 wt.% and C 0.4–1.1 wt.%. (c) maps "A single γ phase region (Y₃)": red at low Al, blue once Al exceeds roughly 10 wt.%, with a visibly irregular boundary. (d) is the combined Y₁+Y₃ intersection (red, Al ≈5–10 wt.%), and (e) the three-way Y₁+Y₂+Y₃ intersection (small red island). A separate cyan curved arrow is annotated "κ fraction ≥ 11.000%". Together the panels argue that intersecting the three screening descriptors isolates a narrow composition window of potentially optimal alloys.

observations.observation: All five composition-space panels (a)–(e) use the same axes: Al(wt.%) on x (ticks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) and C(wt.%) on y (0.0 to 2.2 with 0.2 ticks).
Each panel is a discrete grid of marker points coloured red (criterion satisfied) or blue/black (criterion not satisfied), introduced by a red-circle legend entry with a text label.
In (a) the red region extends across nearly the whole C range for Al above about 5 wt.%, giving a near-vertical red/blue boundary in the Al direction.
The caption and citing text state an Al critical value of 4–4.5 % for the presence of the κ phase, which is lower than the boundary position (≈5 wt.% Al) that the plotted points suggest.
In (b) the red γ+κ dual-phase region is a single enclosed island centred near Al 6–9 wt.% and C 0.4–1.1 wt.%.
The citing text states that the boundary elements of the red region in Fig. 6b are predominantly (4.5–9.3 %) Al and (0.4–1.1 %) C.
In (c) the single-γ-phase (Y₃) red region occupies the low-Al side, with blue appearing once Al exceeds roughly 10 wt.%; the separating boundary is visibly irregular.

The citing text states that the Fig. 6c boundary between the red (Yes) and blue (No) regions fluctuates significantly as the C content escalates to 1.1 %, a value described as critical for austenite stability.
Panel (d) marks the intersection of Y₁ and Y₃ in red, spanning roughly Al 5–10 wt.% over the full C range.
Panel (e) marks the intersection of all three descriptors Y₁+Y₂+Y₃ as a compact red island, visually similar in extent to the Y₂ island in (b).
The citing text states that candidates in the red zone meeting multiple requirements (Y₁, Y₂ and Y₃) are potentially optimal for the system.
A separate cyan curved arrow carries the printed threshold 'κ fraction ≥ 11.000%'.
The caption states the figure represents the first step in screening and that the 30 % Mn two-dimensional search space was used for display because the overall data set is large.

The citing text states that the study found a strong correlation between the presence of the κ phase and the Al element, and that precipitation of κ is primarily governed by Al rather than by C alone.

subfigures.description: Binary composition-space map for 'The existence of the κ phase (Y₁)': x = Al(wt.%) ~1.5–12.5, y = C(wt.%) 0.0–2.2, points red (κ phase present) for Al above roughly 5 wt.% and blue (absent) below, giving a near-vertical red/blue boundary.
Binary map for 'A γ+κ dual-phase region at 500–600 °C (Y₂)'. Same Al/C axes; a single small red island of satisfied points centred near Al 6–9 wt.% and C 0.4–1.1 wt.%, surrounded by blue points.

Binary map for 'A single γ phase region (Y₃)'. Red (single γ region present) at low Al, blue (absent) once Al exceeds roughly 10 wt.%; the red/blue boundary is irregular and wiggles with increasing C.
Combined screening map labelled Y₁+Y₃, red marking compositions satisfying both criteria simultaneously; the red band spans roughly Al 5–10 wt.% across the C range, with black/blue points elsewhere.
Three-way intersection map labelled Y₁+Y₂+Y₃; a small red island of points satisfying all three descriptors, centred near Al 6–9 wt.% and C 0.4–1.1 wt.%, with black/blue points elsewhere.
Cyan curved arrow schematic annotated 'κ fraction ≥ 11.000%', evidently a screening/threshold criterion element accompanying the maps rather than a data panel.

unreadable_items: Exact Al(wt.%) and C(wt.%) coordinates of the red/blue boundaries in (a)–(e) cannot be read to better than the plotted tick spacing; boundary positions are approximate visual estimates between gridlines.
The caption's bracketed panel ordering '(a) (d) (b) (e) (c)' does not match the panel labels visible on the images; the mapping of caption sentences to the bottom cyan-arrow element is uncertain.
The density/overlap of marker points prevents resolving individual data points in the interior of the red and blue regions.
